name: Wellness Hero 01
description: A full-height wellness hero on a warm paper ground: a serif headline and two soft yellow CTAs on the left, a masked bloom photograph bleeding in from the right, and a three-row product table anchored to the bottom edge. Copy, image and table each rise in on their own blurred entrance, and every row and control answers hover with a small, restrained move.

variations.name: default
variations.previewHint: Hover the product rows — the rule warms and the arrow lifts away. Hover either CTA to feel the press.
variations.description: A full-height wellness hero: serif headline, paired yellow CTAs, a mask-faded bloom image on the right, and a product table pinned to the bottom. Entrances are staggered blur-and-rise with motion/react, hover states are spring-free micro-moves, and every animation collapses to a plain fade under reduced motion.

props.description: Desktop nav labels. Hidden below lg, where the menu button takes over.

props.name: heading
props.description: Hero headline. Sized by a clamp that reads both viewport width and height, so it never outgrows a short laptop screen.

props.name: body
props.description: Supporting paragraph under the headline, capped at a 560px measure.

features: Entrances are motion/react rather than CSS keyframes — headline, body, CTA row, image and table each carry their own delay, blur and travel, so the page resolves in one reading order
Hover moves ride variant propagation: the CTA and each product row drive their arrow from the parent, so a single hover target moves two things without a group-hover transform
useReducedMotion swaps every entrance for a plain 0.4s fade and drops hover travel entirely, instead of leaving a half-animated state behind
The bloom is masked by two intersecting gradients, and both the mask and the object-position mirror under rtl, so the image still fades toward the copy in either direction
Padding is written against env(safe-area-inset-*) on every band, so the hero survives a notched phone in landscape
Type and rhythm scale on min(vw, vh) rather than width alone — the headline and product names shrink on a short screen instead of pushing the table off the fold
The table sits on its own upward gradient wash, so it stays readable where the image bleeds behind it
